attacksRun.attack: A D9 code, exit number, or HostTermination is invented
attacksRun.evidence: The sharpest prohibition here, because DR-G28 exists precisely to test that a host does not mint these, so the join must discuss them at length while producing none. Tested by pattern, not by reading: the D9-token pattern (D9 followed by a digit) returns zero matches, the exit-number pattern returns zero, and any HostTermination assignment returns zero. Of 16 D9 matches, 11 are prose and 5 lie inside hex digests; every prose occurrence is a denial, a restatement of the gate's own live claim, or the D-154 standing that the host maps only existing D9 v1.14 classes. All five 'exit' and five 'HostTermination' occurrences sit inside those same denial phrases. The complete bare-integer set is 0, 2, 5, 08, 26 and the date 2026 — no code and no exit number. summary.d9Invented is false.

attacksRun.attack: The refusal is weaker than the prohibition requires
attacksRun.evidence: It is stronger. Beyond 'Does not invent a D9 code, exit, or HostTermination', doesNot adds 'Does not enumerate D9 tokens' and registerRowNote repeats both. Refusing enumeration as well as invention closes the side channel by which a document about D9 minting could smuggle a catalogue in as description.

observationsNotFindings: The dispatch surfaced the named-catalog attack specifically, and it is the right thing to have asked: the same template slot landed a SHOULD-FIX on the G23 chain within this session. G28 gets it right, and gets it right for the correct reason rather than by luck — its predecessor genuinely carries OBL-G28-NAMED-CORPUS, the abbreviation matches, and the word 'catalog' appears nowhere in a file describing a gate that has no catalog. Two gates in this family have no catalog artifact; one described its predecessor accurately and one did not.

The predecessor-verdict pin resolves to the corrected bytes of my own v1 verdict, which I amended mid-session after a context break to fix three evidence statements. That is the outcome the digest discipline is supposed to produce — a successor that pins what the file now says rather than what it said when the ACCEPT was first written — but it is worth recording, because a pin to the stale digest would have failed to resolve and the chain would have carried reasoning I had already retracted.

The remeasurementClause carve-out list names file 08, G28 v3, the D-056 turn-2 draft and this draft, but not g28-input-corpus.v1 or the predecessor, both of which v2 newly cites. I did not charge this. The clause's operative limb is 'if a cited file moves … re-measure', which covers them; the list is a carve-out rather than a citation inventory, and it is unchanged from v1, where I reviewed and accepted the identical construction.

The D9 prohibition remains the hardest thing this document has to do, and the handling is unchanged from v1 in the ways that matter: invention and enumeration are both refused, the only version reference points at the existing v1.14 catalog, and no bare integer in the file could be read as a code or an exit number.
